title: I Forwarded the Bike-Share Overtime Ping After They Docked My Ride as Theirs

parts.text: I ended a ride at 8:44 a.m. and the app still showed me rolling. Dock 17's LED said OCCUPIED by a membership I did not recognize. The terms on the sticker said: END RIDE AT GREEN. OVERTIME FOLLOWS THE SCAN. I was twenty-six, commuter, holding a screenshot of my end tap. A courier in a city vest palmed the bike out and scanned his fob. "Maintenance is always ended." I photographed the LED, the vest, and my end tap. Then I forwarded overtime to support. At 8:51 support asked why a vest fob was on my trip. I have learned the difference between a title and a line item.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Support can see a vest fob on my ended trip with the overtime ping.

social.video_title: He scanned my ended bike onto his vest fob — Part 1/2
social.description: Bike-share, a green I tapped, and a courier's fob. I forwarded overtime. Would you have photographed the LED?

parts.text: The courier called it a rescue until support asked for the stills. I printed the ping, the photo, and the terms. Overtime reversed. He docked with his own fob and told the bay maintenance was always about optics. Optics is a word vests use when a LED exists. Dock policy now has a second line: MAINTENANCE SCANS MAINTENANCE BIKES. I keep my green. He brown-bags the bay. The dock finally looks like a dock, not a second commute. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point. If it is written, it can be applied to the person who wrote it.

social.description: Reversed overtime, stills, and a second line. Was a rescue ever my trip?
